note: The 12 core meanings of Terser. Each has two paraphrased descriptions, so that raters split across option sets and no single wording biases them.

meanings.d1: a causal link: more of the first thing causes more of the second
meanings.d2: a cause-effect link where both move in the same direction

meanings.d1: a causal link: more of the first thing causes less of the second
meanings.d2: a cause-effect link where they move in opposite directions

meanings.d1: a tag marking a feedback loop as self-amplifying (it escalates)
meanings.d2: label for a vicious or virtuous cycle that keeps feeding itself

meanings.d1: a tag marking a feedback loop as goal-seeking: it settles at a target
meanings.d2: label for a self-correcting cycle that stabilises toward a limit

meanings.d1: one quantity is compared with another
meanings.d2: measure the gap between a value and a reference

meanings.d1: movement or flow from one place to the next along a path
meanings.d2: things pass onward, step by step, in a direction

meanings.d1: flow returning to an earlier step (rework or repeat)
meanings.d2: material goes in reverse, upstream to a previous stage

meanings.d1: an effect that arrives late, after a time delay
meanings.d2: there is a waiting period before the consequence shows up

meanings.d1: an accumulated amount that builds up or drains over time
meanings.d2: a reservoir-like quantity holding what has gathered so far

meanings.d1: a flow that adds to an accumulated amount
meanings.d2: an incoming stream that fills a reservoir

meanings.d1: a flow that drains an accumulated amount
meanings.d2: an outgoing stream that empties a reservoir

meanings.d1: work divides into paths that run at the same time (in parallel)
meanings.d2: branches that happen simultaneously, not one after another
